verdict.line: You win if you poke him down with E and force a kill through level 6-8; you lose if the lane stalls and his Q stacks compound into the late game.

brief.thesis: Malphite's short-cooldown, armor-scaling E outtrades Nasus before his stacks matter, which is why Malphite holds lane and solo-kill advantage early. But every minion Nasus last-hits with Q (Siphoning Strike) is a permanent damage increase, so the longer the lane goes uncontested the more the math flips toward him — the 47% win rate across 3,172 games is a lane that opens favored and closes contested.

theirWindow.what: Once Wither (W, 15/14/13/12/11s cooldown) lands on you, your movement and attack speed are cut for its duration. Combined with a high stack count his Q trades will out-damage your E — disengage instead of trading through it.

yourWindow.what: Unstoppable Force (R, 1000 range) lets you charge in from well outside his 255-range Q and knock him up for your jungler to follow up — call for the gank the moment you hit 6, per the matchup's own solo-kill advantage.

start.why: 77.1% pick rate at 46.3% win over 2,999 games — the mana sustains your 8s Q and 7s E so you can poke every cooldown without running dry early.

boots.why: 63.4% pick rate at 47.5% win over 2,347 games — Nasus's entire kit is auto-attacks, so flat reduction on his Siphoning Strike autos matters more than magic resist.

core.why: Highest-winning core path (53.2% over 173 games) — the burn adds free armor-scaling damage and helps you shove waves, denying him free Q last-hits.
Directly punishes Soul Eater lifesteal and stacked-up autos, which is his only damage source once he's farmed stacks.
The attack speed slow aura cuts into his Q-stacking auto rhythm, and the armor further inflates your E's damage output.

situational.when: he rushes lifesteal and is healing through your trades early
their team has heavy magic damage threatening a burst combo onto you
you're ahead and want your R+E combo to delete him before his stacks matter

runes.keystoneWhy: 49.7% win rate over the higher-picked page — the extra health and sustain let you win extended short trades against his Q without losing the HP war before 6.

summoners.why: 71.7% pick rate at 47.6% win — Teleport lets you reset after shoving with E without losing CS to his free farming, and Flash backs up your R engage or bails you out of a Wither chase.

playing.title: Trade with E, not autos
playing.detail: Ground Slam (E, 7s cooldown) deals magic damage off your armor and slows his attack speed — fire it on cooldown in short trades, since it outpaces his Q's 8-4s cooldown range early, then step outside his 255-range Siphoning Strike.

playing.title: Count his stacks all lane
playing.detail: Every Siphoning Strike kill is permanent bonus damage. Don't give him free, uncontested farm windows by overextending your trades — shove the wave and walk, don't duel through minion waves.

playing.title: Call the level 6 gank
playing.detail: Unstoppable Force (R, 1000 range, 130s cooldown at rank 1) lets you engage from outside his Q range — this matches the matchup's own solo-kill edge, so ask your jungler to path top the moment you hit 6.

playing.title: Save W for all-ins
playing.detail: Brutal Strikes (W, 14s cooldown) hits everything in front of you and buffs your armor and AD briefly — hold it for a committed trade or his Wither window, not for poke.

playing.title: Respect Wither
playing.detail: When his W (Wither, 15-11s cooldown) lands, your attack and movement speed drop — disengage rather than trading through it, since it strips the kiting edge your Q slow normally gives you.

playing.title: Finish Thornmail and Frozen Heart on curve
playing.detail: His entire scaling is stacked Q autos plus Soul Eater lifesteal — Thornmail punishes the healing and Frozen Heart's aura slows the autos down, both hitting his power source directly.

playing.title: Don't 1v1 him past 14
playing.detail: Once he's banked enough stacks and Fury of the Sands is up, a straight duel favors him — play for picks with your team or split-push elsewhere instead.

brief.patchCaveat: The build, runes, and summoner spells above come from measured win rates across the cited games on the current patch; the trade timing, cooldown windows, and stack-denial reasoning are my own read of the kit matchup, not sourced from OP.GG.

stats.opponentTip: Do not let Nasus gain stacks by dealing damage. Try to kill him after reaching level 6 though a gank.
